title: When do cheap embeddings beat protein language models? A theoretically-grounded hashing sketch for biological sequence classification
abstract: arXiv:2512.10147v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: \textbf{Motivation:} Pre-trained protein language models (PLMs) such as ESM-2 have become the default representation for biological sequence tasks, but they are computationally heavy and require GPUs both for embedding and for fine-tuning. Whether they are actually necessary for sequence \emph{classification}, as opposed to structure prediction, is rarely tested against strong, principled, lightweight alternatives. This question has direct practical stakes for large-scale genomic surveillance, where embedding millions of sequences on commodity hardware is a recurring bottleneck.\\ \textbf{Results:} We introduce Murmur2Vec, an alignment-free, training-free embedding that aggregates $k$-mer counts into a small hash table via the deterministic MurmurHash function, and we cast it as a randomized sketch of the classical $k$-mer spectrum kernel. translated_title: 廉价嵌入何时能胜过蛋白质语言模型？一种有理论依据的哈希草图方法用于生物序列分类
translated_abstract: 动机：以ESM-2为代表的预训练蛋白质语言模型（PLMs）已成为生物序列任务的标准表示方法，但其计算开销巨大，在嵌入和微调阶段均需要GPU支持。对于序列分类任务（相对于结构预测而言），这些模型是否真正必要，很少有研究将其与强大的、有原则的轻量级替代方案进行对比检验。这一问题在大规模基因组监测中具有直接的实际意义，因为在普通硬件上对数百万条序列进行嵌入是一个反复出现的瓶颈。结果：我们提出了Murmur2Vec，这是一种无需比对、无需训练的嵌入方法，它通过确定性的MurmurHash函数将k-mer计数聚合到小型哈希表中，并将其构建为经典k-mer谱核的一种随机草图。我们提供了完整的理论分析：内积的闭式偏差/方差……
tldr: 提出Murmur2Vec——一种基于MurmurHash的无需比对、无需训练的轻量级序列嵌入方法，具有完整的理论保证，证明在生物序列分类任务中廉价嵌入可以胜过计算昂贵的蛋白质语言模型。
en_tdlr: Murmur2Vec, a theoretically-grounded, alignment-free and training-free hashing sketch of the k-mer spectrum kernel, demonstrates that cheap embeddings can outperform computationally heavy protein language models for biological sequence classification.
